summary_md: **Software Engineering Papers ([@ComputerPapers](https://x.com/ComputerPapers/status/2116289884650422721))** shares *When Relevant Code Is Wrong* ([arXiv 2610.38800](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.38800)), proposing CASE, which checks retrieved code against runtime config, feature flags and architecture to label evidence valid or invalid for agents.

referenced_urls.title: When Relevant Code Is Wrong: Runtime-Aware Context for AI Coding Agents

media.description: Abstract of the runtime-aware context paper.
media.ocr_text: AI coding agents increasingly rely on retrieved code and development history to guide software changes. However, highly relevant artifacts may describe implementations that are inactive or incompatible with the target deployment. Neither semantic similarity nor recency establishes whether retrieved information remains applicable under feature flags, architectural migrations, and deployment-specific configurations. We challenge relevance-oriented retrieval by introducing operational context validity, a task-, deployment-, and time-dependent criterion for determining whether software evidence can legitimately guide implementation decisions. We instantiate this new retrieval principle in CASE, an agent-agnostic framework that connects repository artifacts with runtime configurations and architectural evolution, classifies evidence as valid, invalid, or unknown, and generates context packages distinguishing actionable guidance from historical rationale and unresolved constraints.
